info.title: Astrea API
info.description: Computes accessibility-aware itineraries for ASTREA's Beta Test Plan. Call GET /v0/auth/anonymous (or sign up or sign in) to obtain a token, then send it as the access-token header on every other request.

get.description: This endpoint is public: no `access-token` header is required. The returned token must be sent as the `access-token` header on every other request. The token is a signed JWT that expires after 24 hours: on a `401`, get a new one.

202.description: A new anonymous access token was generated.

get.summary: Compute an itinerary between two points, with the parameters in the query string.
get.description:
Same computation as `POST /v0/itinerary`, for clients that can only send a GET
(shareable link, simple fetch). The query parameters use the same names and formats as
the POST body fields. Requires the `access-token` header (see `GET /v0/auth/anonymous`).

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The starting point: either coordinates as `"lat,lng"` with `.` as the decimal separator, or a free-text address geocoded through Nominatim.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The destination point, in the same formats as `start`.

parameters.name: mobility_profile
parameters.description: The user's mobility profile. Conditions the relevance of the other fields.

parameters.name: wheelchair_width
parameters.description: Wheelchair width in meters. Applies to the Wheelchair profile. The returned path is guaranteed to be wider than this value.

parameters.name: physical_strength
parameters.description: Physical strength of a wheelchair user. Applies to the Wheelchair profile. Determines tolerance to slopes and slightly raised curbs.

parameters.name: is_accompanied
parameters.description: Whether the user is accompanied. Applies to the Wheelchair and Blind profiles. Wheelchair: allows gentle slopes even without physical strength. Blind: if not accompanied, a tactile paving path becomes mandatory.

parameters.name: can_climb_stairs
parameters.description: Whether a person on crutches can climb stairs. Applies to the Crutches profile. true: stairs are acceptable (but not too many/too high). false: no stairs, no raised curbs.

parameters.name: path_preferences
parameters.description: Route preferences for an able-bodied pedestrian. Applies to the Pedestrian profile. Example: `LitStreets | Benches` = 24.

200.description: The account of the user the token belongs to.

delete.summary: Delete the signed-in user's account and mobility profile.
delete.description: Right to erasure (GDPR): the account and the mobility profile are deleted for good. Tokens are stateless and are not revoked, but every `/v0/users/me` route checks that the account still exists and answers `401` otherwise, so the user token gives no access to personal data any more. It can still call the anonymous routes until it expires, like an anonymous token.

204.description: The account and the mobility profile were deleted.

401.description: The access-token header is missing, invalid, expired, or is an anonymous token, or the account of the user token no longer exists.

schema.description: Error body returned for 500 Internal Server Error responses.

schema.description:
Response body for `GET` and `PUT /v0/users/me/profile`: the saved mobility profile.
Only the fields that apply to `mobility_profile` are present.

401.description: The access-token header is missing, invalid, expired, or is an anonymous token, or the account of the user token no longer exists.

schema.description: Error body returned for client errors (400 and 422), with a readable message.

put.summary: Create or replace the signed-in user's mobility profile.
put.description: The whole profile is replaced. `consent` must be `true` (GDPR: the profile is health data). Fields that do not apply to the chosen `mobility_profile` are ignored and not stored, with the same rules as `POST /v0/itinerary`.

schema.description:
Request body for `PUT /v0/users/me/profile`. The fields are the ones of
`POST /v0/itinerary`, with the same names, values and rules, so a saved profile can be
sent as is to compute an itinerary. Fields that do not apply to the chosen
`mobility_profile` are ignored and not stored.

Response body for `GET` and `PUT /v0/users/me/profile`: the saved mobility profile.
Only the fields that apply to `mobility_profile` are present.

400.description: A field is invalid, the consent was not given, or the wheelchair model is not in the catalog.

schema.description: Error body returned for 500 Internal Server Error responses.

delete.summary: Delete the signed-in user's mobility profile and withdraw the consent.
delete.description: Withdrawal of the consent (GDPR): the mobility profile and the consent date are deleted for good, the account is kept. The user can save a new profile later with `PUT /v0/users/me/profile`, which asks for the consent again. Deleting a profile that does not exist also answers `204`.

204.description: The mobility profile and the consent were deleted.

401.description: The access-token header is missing, invalid, expired, or is an anonymous token, or the account of the user token no longer exists.

schema.description: Error body returned for 500 Internal Server Error responses.

get.summary: List the standard wheelchairs and the accessibility reference values.
get.description:
Requires the `access-token` header (see `GET /v0/auth/anonymous`).
Use it to build the wheelchair selector, then send the chosen model's
`recommended_wheelchair_width` as `wheelchair_width` to `POST /v0/itinerary`.
All dimensions are in meters.

schema.description: Response body for `GET /v0/wheelchairs`.

401.description: The access-token header is missing or invalid.

schema.description: Error body returned for 500 Internal Server Error responses.

min_passage_width.description: Minimum free passage width, in meters.

recommended_corridor_width.description: Recommended free passage width in corridors, in meters.

turning_circle_diameter.description: Diameter of the circle needed to turn around, in meters.

AccessibilityStandardsResponse.description: Spatial accessibility reference values, in meters.

start.description: The starting point: either coordinates as `"lat,lng"` with `.` as the decimal separator, or a free-text address geocoded through Nominatim.

end.description: The destination point, in the same formats as `start`.

mobility_profile.description: The user's mobility profile. Conditions the relevance of the other fields.

wheelchair_width.description: Wheelchair width in meters. Applies to the Wheelchair profile. The returned path is guaranteed to be wider than this value.

physical_strength.description: Physical strength of a wheelchair user. Applies to the Wheelchair profile. Determines tolerance to slopes and slightly raised curbs.

is_accompanied.description: Whether the user is accompanied. Applies to the Wheelchair and Blind profiles. Wheelchair: allows gentle slopes even without physical strength. Blind: if not accompanied, a tactile paving path becomes mandatory.

can_climb_stairs.description: Whether a person on crutches can climb stairs. Applies to the Crutches profile. true: stairs are acceptable (but not too many/too high). false: no stairs, no raised curbs.

path_preferences.description: Route preferences for an able-bodied pedestrian. Applies to the Pedestrian profile. Example: `LitStreets | Benches` = 24.

CreateItineraryRequest.description: Request body for `POST /v0/itinerary`, and query string for `GET /v0/itinerary` (same snake_case names).

error.description: Human-readable description of what was wrong with the request.

ErrorResponse.description: Error body returned for client errors (400 and 422), with a readable message.

points.description: The computed route, as an ordered list of points from start to end.

email.description: Email address of the account. Compared without case.

MobilityProfile.description: The user's mobility profile. Determines which optional fields on `CreateItineraryRequest` are relevant. (0 = Pedestrian, 1 = Wheelchair, 2 = Crutches, 3 = Blind)

PathPreference.description: Route preferences for able-bodied pedestrians. Combinable bit flags, e.g. `LitStreets | Benches` = 24. Bitmask: Stairs=1, Slopes=2, WidePathways=4, LitStreets=8, Benches=16. Combine with bitwise OR, e.g. LitStreets | Benches = 24.

PhysicalStrength.description: Physical strength level, used for wheelchair users. Determines tolerance to slopes and slightly raised curbs. (0 = Low, 1 = Medium, 2 = High)

email.description: Email address used to sign in. Compared without case.

password.description: At least 8 characters. Stored as a hash, never in clear text.

birth_date.description: Date of birth, ISO format `YYYY-MM-DD`. Must be in the past.

RegisterRequest.description: Request body for `POST /v0/auth/register`. No consent is asked here: the account holds no health data.

error.description: Human-readable error message. Do not rely on its exact wording.

errorId.description: Unique identifier for this error. Quote it to the backend team when reporting an issue: it identifies the corresponding entry in the `error_logs` MongoDB collection.

ServerErrorResponse.description: Error body returned for 500 Internal Server Error responses.

accessToken.description: The access token (JWT). Send it as the `access-token` header on every other request.

TokenResponse.description:
Response body for `GET /v0/auth/anonymous`, `POST /v0/auth/register` and
`POST /v0/auth/login`. The expiry is in the `exp` claim of the token.

consent.description: Consent to store the mobility profile, which is health data (GDPR). Must be `true`, otherwise the request is refused with a 400. Withdraw it with `DELETE /v0/users/me/profile`.

app_profile.description: Free value stored for the apps and never used by the API, to restore the choice made in the form when several app choices share the same `mobility_profile` (for example stroller and pedestrian are both 0).

mobility_profile.description: The user's mobility profile. Conditions the relevance of the other fields.

wheelchair_model_id.description: Id of the chosen model in `GET /v0/wheelchairs`. Wheelchair profile only. Optional: a user can enter a width without choosing a model. When it is set and `wheelchair_width` is not, the model's `recommended_wheelchair_width` is stored.

wheelchair_width.description: Wheelchair width in meters. Wheelchair profile only.

physical_strength.description: Physical strength of a wheelchair user. Wheelchair profile only.

is_accompanied.description: Whether the user is accompanied. Wheelchair and Blind profiles only.

can_climb_stairs.description: Whether a person on crutches can climb stairs. Crutches profile only.

path_preferences.description: Route preferences, bitmask. Pedestrian profile only.

UserProfileRequest.description:
Request body for `PUT /v0/users/me/profile`. The fields are the ones of
`POST /v0/itinerary`, with the same names, values and rules, so a saved profile can be
sent as is to compute an itinerary. Fields that do not apply to the chosen
`mobility_profile` are ignored and not stored.

consent.description: Always `true`: a profile is only stored with the consent.

mobility_profile.description: The user's mobility profile. Determines which optional fields on `CreateItineraryRequest` are relevant.

consent_given_at.description: When the user gave the consent to store the profile. Kept when the profile is replaced; set again after a withdrawal.

UserProfileResponse.description:
Response body for `GET` and `PUT /v0/users/me/profile`: the saved mobility profile.
Only the fields that apply to `mobility_profile` are present.

UserResponse.description: Response body for `GET /v0/users/me`: the signed-in user's account.

items.description: A wheelchair category and its standard models.

categories.description: The wheelchair categories (manual, electric), each with its standard models.

accessibility_standards.description: Reference values for designing navigable routes and spaces.

id.description: Stable identifier of the category, to use as a translation key on the client.

name.description: English display name of the category.

items.description: A standard wheelchair model (brand and range) with its overall dimensions.

models.description: The standard models of this category.

WheelchairCategoryResponse.description: A wheelchair category and its standard models.

id.description: Stable identifier of the model. Store this, not the label, to remember the user's choice.

range.description: Product ranges covered by this entry.

length.description: Overall length range, in meters. Informational: the engine does not use it yet.

recommended_wheelchair_width.description: Width in meters to send as `wheelchair_width` to `POST /v0/itinerary`. It is the widest chair of the range, so the returned path fits every chair of the range.

WheelchairModelResponse.description: A standard wheelchair model (brand and range) with its overall dimensions.

accessToken.description: Access token (JWT) obtained from GET /v0/auth/anonymous, POST /v0/auth/register or POST /v0/auth/login. Send it as the access-token header on every other request.
accessToken.name: access-token
